researcher_ranking.sc_overview_desc: This ranking system is designed to evaluate researchers' qualitative excellence from multiple perspectives.
researcher_ranking.sc_overview_core: Core Indicators (80 pts): Directly measure research impact and quality (FWCI, citations, journal level, intl collaboration)
researcher_ranking.sc_overview_secondary: Secondary Indicators (10 pts): Assess social value and accessibility (SDG, OA, trending topics)
researcher_ranking.sc_method_title: Scoring Method: Average of Per-Paper Scores
researcher_ranking.sc_method_desc: Each indicator calculates a score for each individual paper, then computes the average across all papers.
researcher_ranking.sc_method_note: Only FWCI allows median/mean selection: Median is recommended to reduce impact of extreme high-citation papers.
researcher_ranking.sc_fwci_def: Definition: Ratio of paper citations to world average for same year, field, and document type
researcher_ranking.sc_top_cited_def: Definition: Whether paper is in top 10% by citations within same year and field
researcher_ranking.sc_top_cited_meaning: Meaning: Most cited excellent papers in the field
researcher_ranking.sc_top_journal_def: Definition: Paper published in journal ranked top 10% by SNIP, CiteScore, or SJR
researcher_ranking.sc_top_journal_meaning: Meaning: Published in the most influential journals in the field
researcher_ranking.sc_snip_desc: SNIP: Source Normalized Impact per Paper (field-normalized citations)
researcher_ranking.sc_citescore_desc: CiteScore: Citations in 4 years / Papers in same period
researcher_ranking.sc_intl_def: Definition: FWCI of papers co-authored with researchers from foreign institutions
researcher_ranking.sc_intl_meaning: Meaning: Quality assessment of international collaborative research
researcher_ranking.sc_intl_note: Note: 0 points if no international papers (excluded from average calculation)
researcher_ranking.sc_sdg_def: Definition: Papers related to UN Sustainable Development Goals
researcher_ranking.sc_sdg_meaning: Meaning: Social value and contribution of research
researcher_ranking.sc_oa_def: Definition: Open access papers freely available to everyone
researcher_ranking.sc_oa_meaning: Meaning: Openness and accessibility of research output
researcher_ranking.sc_prom_def: Definition: Academic attention percentile of SciVal Topic
researcher_ranking.sc_prom_note: Based on recent citations, views, Mendeley saves, etc.
researcher_ranking.sc_secondary_example_desc: Secondary indicators also calculate average of per-paper scores like core indicators.
researcher_ranking.sc_secondary_sum_example: Secondary subtotal: SDG(1.2) + OA(1.5) + Prominence(3.33) = 6.03 pts (max 10 pts)
researcher_ranking.sc_total_formula: Total = FWCI + Top10%Cited + TopJournal + IntlCollabFWCI + SDG + OA + Prominence
researcher_ranking.sc_note1: Target: Scopus-indexed papers and JBNU primary-affiliated researchers
researcher_ranking.sc_note2: Period filter: Real-time recalculation using only papers in the selected period
researcher_ranking.sc_note3: FWCI calculation: Choose between 'Median' and 'Mean' (Median recommended)
researcher_ranking.sc_note4: Tie-breaker: Higher FWCI value ranks higher
researcher_ranking.biblio_h_def: The largest number h such that h publications have at least h citations each
researcher_ranking.biblio_h_method_desc: Sort papers by citation count in descending order; h is the largest rank where rank ≤ citation count
researcher_ranking.biblio_h_example: h=10 means at least 10 papers have been cited 10+ times each
researcher_ranking.biblio_h_strength: Balanced measure of productivity and impact
researcher_ranking.biblio_g_def: The largest number g such that the top g papers have at least g² total citations
researcher_ranking.biblio_g_method_desc: The largest g where the sum of citations of the top g papers is not less than g²
researcher_ranking.biblio_g_example: g=15 means the top 15 papers have at least 225 total citations
researcher_ranking.biblio_g_strength: Better reflects highly-cited papers than h-index
researcher_ranking.biblio_i10_def: Number of publications with 10 or more citations
researcher_ranking.biblio_i10_example: i10=20 means 20 papers have been cited 10+ times
researcher_ranking.biblio_i10_strength: Intuitive and easy to understand (Google Scholar metric)
researcher_ranking.alert_no_data: No data available. Please search first.
researcher_ranking.biblio_m_def: h-index divided by the number of years of academic activity
researcher_ranking.biblio_m_strength: Fairly compares early-career and senior researchers by accounting for career length

analysis_modules.formula_growth:
▶ Formula
• Growth Rate = (Recent 3yr papers / Total papers) × 100
• Total Score = Growth Rate × 0.4 + FWCI × 20 + Recent 3yr papers × 2
• Target: 5+ years career & 10+ papers

▶ Example
Researcher A: Total 20, Recent 3yr 12, FWCI 2.5
• Growth Rate = (12 / 20) × 100 = 60%
• Total Score = 60 × 0.4 + 2.5 × 20 + 12 × 2 = 24 + 50 + 24 = 98 pts
analysis_modules.formula_high_fwci_low_output:
▶ Formula
• Efficiency Score = FWCI × 100 / Paper count
• Target: 5-30 papers with FWCI ≥ 1.5
• High efficiency = High impact with fewer papers

▶ Example
Researcher B: 8 papers, FWCI 3.2
• Efficiency = 3.2 × 100 / 8 = 40 pts
Researcher C: 25 papers, FWCI 2.0
• Efficiency = 2.0 × 100 / 25 = 8 pts
→ Researcher B has higher efficiency
analysis_modules.formula_high_prominence:
▶ Formula
• High Prom Count = Papers with Prominence ≥ 90%
• Max Prom = Highest Prominence percentile
• Main Topics = Topic Cluster names of high-prom papers

▶ Example
Researcher D: 10 papers
• Prominence values: 95%, 92%, 88%, 85%, 91%, 72%, 65%, 93%, 45%, 80%
• High Prom Count = 4 papers (95%, 92%, 91%, 93%)
• Max Prom = 95%
analysis_modules.formula_top_journal_low_citation:
▶ Formula
• Top Journal % = (Top 10% journal papers / Total) × 100
• Expected Citations = Top journal papers × Field avg citations
• Citation Gap = Actual - Expected (lower = more potential)

▶ Example
Researcher E: 15 total, 6 in top journals, 120 actual citations
• Top Journal% = (6 / 15) × 100 = 40%
• Field avg 35 citations/paper → Expected = 6 × 35 = 210
• Citation Gap = 120 - 210 = -90 (improvement potential)
analysis_modules.formula_intl_collab_potential:
▶ Formula
• Intl Collab = Papers with is_international=1
• Intl Ratio = Intl papers / Total × 100
• Intl FWCI = Average FWCI of intl papers
• Target: FWCI median ≥ 1.0, Intl ratio < 30%

▶ Example
Researcher F: 20 total, 4 intl papers, FWCI median 1.8
• Intl Ratio = (4 / 20) × 100 = 20% (<30% → eligible)
• Intl paper FWCIs: 2.1, 1.8, 2.5, 1.9
• Intl FWCI = (2.1+1.8+2.5+1.9) / 4 = 2.08
analysis_modules.formula_top_journal_no_top_cited:
▶ Formula
• Top Journal % = Top 10% journal publication rate
• Top Cited = Papers with is_top_cited=1
• Target: Has top journal experience but 0 top-cited papers

▶ Example
Researcher G: 12 total papers
• Top 10% journal papers: 5 → Top Journal% = 41.7%
• Top 10% cited papers: 0
→ Has journal capability but needs citation strategy
analysis_modules.formula_no_intl_high_performer:
▶ Formula
• Intl Collab = Intl papers (0-2 papers)
• Top Journal % = Top 10% journal rate
• Target: FWCI median ≥ 1.0 & ≤ 2 intl papers

▶ Example
Researcher H: 18 total, 1 intl paper, FWCI median 1.5
• Top journal papers: 7 → Top Journal% = (7/18)×100 = 38.9%
• Intl Collab = 1 (≤2 → eligible)
→ High potential with intl collaboration expansion
analysis_modules.formula_collab_high_citation:
▶ Formula
• Intl Collab = Intl papers (5+ required)
• Intl Ratio = Intl papers / Total × 100
• Intl FWCI = Average FWCI of intl papers
• Target: 5+ intl papers & FWCI median ≥ 1.5

▶ Example
Researcher I: 25 total, 12 intl papers, FWCI median 2.1
• Intl Ratio = (12/25)×100 = 48%
• Intl papers avg FWCI = 2.8
→ Suitable as mentor/role model
analysis_modules.formula_field_hub:
▶ Formula
• Field = ASJC academic field name
• Field Papers = Papers in that field
• Coauthors = Unique coauthors in field
• Top 3 by coauthor count per field

▶ Example
Researcher J: 'Materials Science' field
• Field Papers = 15
• Unique Coauthors = 42 (no duplicates)
→ Extensive collaboration network in field

research_strategy.title: Research Strategy
research_strategy.subtitle: Research trends and strategic analysis
research_strategy.strategic_portfolio_desc: Analyze field strengths and growth potential
research_strategy.decision_growth_trajectory: Selection of priority funding recipients, identification of continuous growth program candidates, evidence for excellent researcher incentives
research_strategy.decision_early_warning: Selection of research environment improvement support targets, identification of sabbatical/overseas training candidates, priority determination for investigating research activity decline causes
research_strategy.decision_rising_star: Selection for junior researcher development programs, senior-junior mentoring matching, identification of excellent junior researcher incentive targets
research_strategy.decision_patent_cited: Selection of technology transfer/commercialization support targets, support for patent-linked research activation, identification of industry-academia collaboration excellence awards
research_strategy.decision_policy_cited: Awards/support for researchers with high social impact, identification of policy advisory committee recommendation candidates, evidence for social contribution research activation support
research_strategy.decision_sdg_contribution: Support for SDG-related research activation, awards for UN SDG contributing researchers, identification of candidates for SDG-related international cooperation/external projects
research_strategy.decision_field_strategy_map: Determining field investment priorities, establishing strategies for core strengths/development needs, setting internationalization strategy directions by field
research_strategy.decision_collab_effect: Securing justification for international cooperation program investment, identifying optimal collaboration types per researcher, basis for selecting international cooperation support targets
research_strategy.decision_academic_corporate: Awards/support for industry-academia collaboration excellent researchers, identification of industry-academia-research program participation candidates, selection of corporate joint research expansion targets
research_strategy.insights_growth_trajectory: Identifies researchers with steadily increasing annual publications over the past 3 years ({y1}~{y3}). Quantitatively compares growth trend intensity (growth rate) to confirm core research personnel showing continuous growth.
research_strategy.insights_early_warning: Identifies researchers with 50%+ publication decline in recent 2 years ({y4}~{y5}) compared to past 3 years ({y1}~{y3}). Determines support urgency by decline rate size and early detection of those needing research environment improvement.
research_strategy.insights_rising_star: Identifies excellent junior researchers within 5 years of first publication who achieved FWCI > 1.5 or h-index >= 5. Confirms future core researcher candidates showing high research capability relative to short career.
research_strategy.insights_patent_cited: Identifies researchers whose work has been cited in patents. Confirms researchers with high technology transfer and commercialization potential and patent citation scale.
research_strategy.insights_policy_cited: Identifies researchers whose work has been cited in policy documents. Compares researchers substantively contributing to social policy formulation and the magnitude of policy influence.
research_strategy.insights_sdg_contribution: Identifies researchers conducting research contributing to UN SDGs. Confirms researcher distribution by SDG goal and multi-field SDG contributing researchers.
research_strategy.insights_field_strategy_map: Assesses JBNU's field-by-field research competitiveness based on ASJC field publications, average FWCI, and international collaboration ratio. Confirms field positioning (core strength/growth/scale advantage/needs development) and qualitative-quantitative balance.
research_strategy.insights_collab_effect: Analyzes FWCI differences by collaboration type (single/institutional/domestic/international) per researcher. Quantitatively confirms the effect of international collaboration on citation performance and compares FWCI by collaboration type.
research_strategy.insights_academic_corporate: Analyzes researchers with industry-academia (academic+corporate co-affiliation) papers. Assesses the qualitative performance (FWCI) of industry-academia papers and each researcher's industry-academia collaboration intensity.

research_strategy.formula_field_avg_fwci: Sum of field papers FWCI / paper count (JBNU field average)
research_strategy.formula_top_journal_ratio: is_1=1 (Top 10% journal) papers / total papers x 100
research_strategy.formula_total_citations: Sum of citations for field papers

research_strategy.formula_corp_fwci: Sum of corp papers FWCI / corp paper count (average FWCI)
